updates.title: AWS offers OpenAI Daybreak Red in GovCloud (US-East) to eligible customers
updates.whatChanged: On 30 October, AWS made OpenAI Daybreak Red, also called GPT-5.6 Cyber, available to eligible customers on Amazon Bedrock in AWS GovCloud (US-East). OpenAI's Trusted Access for Cyber enrollment and AWS account-team approval gate access. AWS says inference data is not used to train models.
updates.whyCare: Security teams can run a model built for defensive vulnerability work with Bedrock's identity and data controls. Only approved customers can access it.
updates.before: Before this launch, AWS had not listed Daybreak Red as available in GovCloud.
updates.after: Eligible customers can request Daybreak Red in GovCloud (US-East) after OpenAI's Trusted Access for Cyber enrollment and AWS account-team approval.
updates.learn: Confirm Trusted Access for Cyber eligibility and AWS's approval path. Check automated abuse-detection retention and the zero-data-retention request path before sending sensitive inputs. Evaluate the model only on authorized defensive tasks.

sources.name: AWS What's New - OpenAI Daybreak Red in GovCloud
AWS Machine Learning Blog - Daybreak Red and Daybreak Blue on Amazon Bedrock

updates.architectureImplication: Treat Daybreak Red as a separately gated option for defensive cyber workflows. Compare its access checks, Bedrock isolation and retention terms with approved hosted models and self-hosted open weights.
heldReasons: Fact check: The item says AWS account-team approval is an access gate | The sources require OpenAI enrollment and say to contact the AWS account team to request or enable access after approval, but do not say the AWS team itself approves eligibility.
